issue_context.title: kube-proxy node IP / bind address does not fall back to 127.0.0.1 anymore in iptables mode when node is missing from API
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->

**What happened**:

Using Kubernetes 1.16.1, I started kube-proxy in iptables mode as a static pod on a master node. The master node was intentionally (and permanently) not available in the API as a Node object.

kube-proxy started up and terminated soon after because it failed to [fetch the Node from the API](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.16.1/pkg/util/node/node.go#L112-L138) (which is supposed to function as the bound address) and eventually returned an error:

```
E1011 15:25:45.275305       1 node.go:124] Failed to retrieve node info: nodes "master-k8s-1-16" not found
E1011 15:25:46.414712       1 node.go:124] Failed to retrieve node info: nodes "master-k8s-1-16" not found
E1011 15:25:48.557554       1 node.go:124] Failed to retrieve node info: nodes "master-k8s-1-16" not found
E1011 15:25:52.953709       1 node.go:124] Failed to retrieve node info: nodes "master-k8s-1-16" not found
E1011 15:26:01.612814       1 node.go:124] Failed to retrieve node info: nodes "master-k8s-1-16" not found
F1011 15:26:01.612866       1 server.go:443] unable to get node IP for hostname master-k8s-1-16
```

**What you expected to happen**:

I expected the same behavior as in Kubernetes 1.15 where failure to look up the Node in the API would result in [127.0.0.1 to be used as the default bind address when iptables mode is used](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.15.4/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L315-L318).

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Configure kube-proxy with iptables mode on Kubernetes 1.16 without the hosting Node being available in the Kubernetes API (under the OS hostname).

**Anything else we need to know?**:

PR #77167 (_Fix for kube-proxy to wait for some duration for the node to be defined_) introduced an additional [check for the node IP and returns an error if it is found empty](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/77167/files#diff-934760ea1a4e195e49bcd10625cf4e46R146-R148). I believe this is the part that is causing the change in behavior: in Kubernetes 1.15, the check would be omitted and cause `iptables.NewProxier()` to set the default bind address to 127.0.0.1 (when iptables mode is set; I haven't checked other modes).

The PR's primary purpose seems to be a different one (retrying node IP retrieval from the API), so my understanding is that the added check was not really needed; unless I'm misunderstanding things which I don't want to rule out at all. 

The quick workaround was to explicitly configure kube-proxy with `--bind-address 127.0.0.1`. However, I'm not entirely sure if that's a good solution long-term compared to letting Kubernetes do The Right Thing, which is what I'd like to clarify through this issue.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.16.1
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: Kubernetes running on DigitalOcean VMs (droplets)
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Debian GNU/Linux 9 (stretch)
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux master-k8s-1-16-test1 4.19.0-0.bpo.6-amd64 #1 SMP Debian 4.19.67-2+deb10u1~bpo9+1 (2019-09-30) x86_64 GNU/Linux

/sig network

/cc @paulsubrata55 @thockin who were involved in the referenced PR.
comments:
I made a similar comment in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/77167#discussion_r336275761, wondering if this is a breaking change in v1.16 that we should revert? 

Previously if `nodeIP` is nil, kube-proxy defaults to [127.0.0.1 as the node IP](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L282-L286) but now kube-proxy always exits with error instead of defaulting to local host. I think a lot of external cloud providers relied on this behavior because they needed to talk to API server prior to node addresses being set by the provider. 

Thoughts @thockin? 

/assign @thockin
Opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84071 to preserve behavior before v1.16 where node IP defaults to 127.0.01 is none is found. PTAL

review_comments: The proxier implementations already sets node IP to 127.0.0.1 if it's nil, wondering if it makes more sense to remove this nil check altogether (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84071 -- closed in favor of this PR).

This change _may_ now impact `ipvs.NewProxier()` (I can't tell for sure currently as I'm on mobile only) which used to not necessarily come with a set node IP.

Is there a reason we cannot just drop line 140 without adding anything else? That's what the code originally used to do, so it seems like the cleaner approach to me with regards to addressing the bug.

Should we remove the code in NewProxier implementations that checks for and handles nil?  This is kind of a contract change - they can assume it is non-nil.

So I guess from a compat POV this is correct.  From a correctness POV, this is wrong.  At least the iptables module will make a wrong decision based on this information.  IPVS seems only to log it.

Having the user set the --bind-address seems like the RIGHT answer, but I acknowledge that this is a breaking change and we should fix it.

Can we enhance the log message to say something like:
````
    klog.V(0).Infof("can't determine this node's IP, assuming 127.0.0.1; if this is incorrect, set the --bind-address flag")
```

Of course, flags are passe and config files are vogue, and it's harder to reference config file fields.  This is also wrongish in the case of IPv6.

> Should we remove the code in NewProxier implementations that checks for and handles nil? This is kind of a contract change - they can assume it is non-nil.

If  iptables.NewProxier was only used here, it might be redundant to validate nodeIP `nil` again. But, I found that it was used by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubemark/hollow_proxy.go#L82, so I withdrew the modification here
Can we fix that do explicitly pass 127.0.0.1 and remove it from NewProxier?

> Can we fix that do explicitly pass 127.0.0.1 and remove it from NewProxier?

Done.PTAL

This has been present for ~4 years (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/1acaa1db09e96d297255270ecb1cf29791615fdf#diff-d51765b83fe795b469e8a86276b12dc9R218-R221). Can you explain why this is correct to remove?

@liggitt I think https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/77167 introduced a breaking change where kube-proxy exits if nodeIP is nil. Before v1.16, if nodeIP is nil kube-proxy continues assuming later it would default node IP to 127.0.0.1.

> This has been present for ~4 years ([1acaa1d#diff-d51765b83fe795b469e8a86276b12dc9R218-R221](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/1acaa1db09e96d297255270ecb1cf29791615fdf#diff-d51765b83fe795b469e8a86276b12dc9R218-R221)). Can you explain why this is correct to remove?

At first, I thought that `iptables.NewProxier` was only used here, if so, it might be redundant to validate `nodeIP` again. Later, I found that it was used by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubemark/hollow_proxy.go#L82, so I withdrew the modification here
How is this different from simply rolling back #77167 ?  I thought the point of that was to force kube-proxy not to proceed with a wrong IP address?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/77167 also adds exponential back-off which fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/37414 where kube-proxy would try to get the node IP before the node is registered. IMO removing the nodeIP check entirely and having the proxy implementations fall back to use 127.0.0.1 is better.
